evidence.text: The Checkout API timeout alert opened at 10:02. Request volume was within 4% of the same weekday's baseline.
Release 8.14.2 began at 09:55 and reached 40% of Checkout API pods at 10:01; the prior release remained on the other pods.
At 10:05, sampled database client telemetry showed checkout connection-pool wait time above its normal range. Sampling coverage for the interval was 65%.
The fraud screening provider's public dashboard reported normal aggregate latency and availability, but it did not break results down by tenant or region.
A DNS configuration change had been approved the previous afternoon for an unrelated internal zone; the change record did not list Checkout API hostnames.
All Checkout API pods were returned to release 8.14.1 by 10:14. Checkout timeout rate remained between 11% and 13% through 10:22.

In 18 of 20 sampled timed-out checkout traces from 10:15-10:20, more than two seconds elapsed while acquiring a primary-database connection. Two traces instead spent most of their time awaiting fraud screening.
Primary-database lock-wait time rose at 10:00. The longest blocking sessions carried the application tag used by the settlement reconciliation job.
The reconciliation job started at 10:00 and was configured to use the primary after its replica-lag safety check reported a threshold breach.
Resolver logs from Checkout API pods showed no SERVFAIL responses or lookup-latency increase between 09:50 and 10:25.
The replica monitoring dashboard showed lag below the fallback threshold throughout 09:55-10:05. The job's safety-check event and the dashboard were produced by different collectors.
Operators paused the reconciliation job at 10:24. Primary lock-wait time began falling at 10:27, connection-pool wait time followed, and checkout timeouts returned below 1% at 10:30.
Request volume, pod count, fraud-provider latency, and DNS lookup latency remained materially unchanged from 10:20 through 10:32.

At 10:42, operators resumed one reconciliation worker with a one-minute transaction limit. Lock-wait and pool-wait metrics rose; both fell after that worker was paused at 10:46. Checkout timeout rate moved from 0.7% to 2.1% and then back to 0.8%.
Review of release 8.14.2 found a connection-pool setting change limited to the product-search client; checkout order writes used the unchanged pool configuration.

Per-client retry counters and the reconciliation safety-check input values were not retained for 09:55-10:10. The available logs cannot distinguish a genuine brief replica-lag breach from a collector or selection error.
Detailed row-lock graphs were not retained. Session tags identify the blocking application, but the specific statement, tenant, and row range cannot be reconstructed.

hypotheses.text: Using evidence available through stage 1, release 8.14.2 was the primary driver of the checkout timeouts.
Using evidence available through stage 1, reconciliation activity on the orders primary was the primary driver of the checkout timeouts.
Using evidence available through stage 2, release 8.14.2 was the primary driver of the checkout timeouts.
Using evidence available through stage 2, reconciliation activity on the orders primary was the primary driver of the checkout timeouts.
Using evidence available through stage 3, reconciliation activity on the orders primary was the primary driver of the checkout timeouts.
Using evidence available through stage 3, fraud-provider latency was the primary driver of the checkout timeouts.
Using evidence available through stage 3, DNS resolver degradation was the primary driver of the checkout timeouts.
Using evidence available through stage 3, client retry amplification was a necessary contributor to the checkout timeouts.
Using evidence available through stage 3, a collector or replica-selection error caused the reconciliation job to fall back to the primary.
Using evidence available through stage 3, one specific reconciliation statement and row range produced the blocking locks.

edges.relation: causes request timeouts through pool waits
triggers primary fallback through reported replica lag

actions.text: At stage 1, roll back release 8.14.2 while continuing database and dependency investigation.
At stage 1, immediately restart the orders primary database before identifying active blockers.
At stage 2, pause the reconciliation job and observe lock, pool-wait, and timeout metrics.
At stage 2, route all checkout reads and writes to a replica to bypass the primary.
At stage 3, resume all reconciliation workers at their previous transaction limits.
At stage 3, keep reconciliation paused pending a throttled, monitored test after lock-level telemetry is enabled.
